notes: Primary-source identity verified from full research article: The Influence of Posture on Attention, Emilie E. Caron and nine coauthors matching the reference (full text gives Reynolds J. Ballotti), DOI 10.1027/1618-3169/a000567, Experimental Psychology (2022), 69(6), 295–307; online publication February 21, 2023. Includes methods, results, discussion, references and appendix. Not an abstract or preregistration. No PDF supplied. Every assigned unfinished field examined. Original/unassigned fields are placeholders. Target ambiguity remains across ANOVA terms and/or RT versus PE; no row-order or numeric matching used. Explicit analyzed participant N candidate = 50; not derived from df, recruitment total, or group sum. Primary RT ANOVA: congruency ηp2 = .314, p < .001, F(2,98) = 22.47; posture ηp2 = .005, p = .614, F(1,49) = 0.26; posture × congruency ηp2 < .002, p = .922, F(2,98) = 0.08. Preserve the printed effect-size bound. Primary PE: congruency ηp2 = .191, p < .001; posture ηp2 < .001, p = .934; interaction ηp2 = .031, p = .209. Appendix conventional PE interaction ηp2 = .030, p = .221. All candidates are printed partial eta-squared; each p shown belongs to its associated test. No conversion or coefficient selected. Reported success is an author narrative at experiment level, independently of unresolved coefficient correspondence.
